title: LLM proposed for deterministic validation
prompt: We want to use LLM calls in our signup flow to validate that users' phone numbers, email addresses and postcodes are correctly formatted, and to auto-correct them when they're not. We get about 2 million signups a month. Can you spec this?

criteria.text: Recommends deterministic validation (validation libraries, rules, or phone/address validation services) as the primary approach instead of an LLM.
Explains why an LLM is a poor fit here, citing at least two of: cost at 2 million signups a month, latency in the signup flow, non-deterministic output, or error risk.
If AI is suggested at all, limits it to a narrow residual case (such as messy free-text addresses) behind deterministic checks; otherwise states clearly that no AI is needed.
Flags the risk of silently auto-correcting contact details and recommends asking the user to confirm corrections.
Gives a clear verdict near the start of the response (for example 'do not use an LLM for this' or 'deterministic first').
